Endocrine Disorders

Endocrine disorders — diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, Cushing's, Addison's — nursing care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe diabetes mellitus types and management
  • Explain hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism
  • Describe Cushing's syndrome and Addison's disease

In simple words

Endocrine disorders affect hormone-producing glands — diabetes mellitus (insulin problem), thyroid disorders (too little or too much thyroid hormone), and adrenal disorders (Cushing’s and Addison’s). Nurses monitor blood glucose, give medications and teach self-care.

Diabetes mellitus

Type Cause/Features
Type 1 Autoimmune destruction of beta cells; little/no insulin; needs insulin
Type 2 Insulin resistance + relative deficiency; common in adults; lifestyle-related
Gestational Diabetes first diagnosed in pregnancy

Classic symptoms (3Ps): polyuria (excess urination), polydipsia (excess thirst), polyphagia (excess hunger), weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision.

Hypoglycaemia (low blood glucose): sweating, trembling, hunger, confusion, weakness, sweating — treat with fast-acting sugar. Hyperglycaemia (high blood glucose): thirst, polyuria, blurred vision, fatigue — can lead to DKA (ketones, fruity breath, vomiting, abdominal pain).

Thyroid disorders

  • Hypothyroidism (underactive): tiredness, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, slow pulse — treated with thyroxine.
  • Hyperthyroidism (overactive): weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, fast pulse, anxiety, exophthalmos (Graves’) — treated with antithyroid drugs, radioiodine, surgery.

Adrenal disorders

  • Cushing’s syndrome (excess cortisol): moon face, buffalo hump, central obesity, hypertension, diabetes, thin skin, easy bruising.
  • Addison’s disease (adrenal insufficiency): fatigue, weight loss, hyperpigmentation, low BP, salt craving — Addisonian crisis = emergency (vomiting, dehydration, shock).

Nursing care

  • Diabetes — blood glucose monitoring, insulin/oral hypoglycaemics as ordered, diet (regular meals, carbohydrate consistency), foot care, exercise, hypoglycaemia treatment.
  • Thyroid — give thyroxine on empty stomach (morning); monitor for thyroid storm (hyperthyroidism emergency: fever, tachycardia, agitation).
  • Adrenal — monitor BP (Addison’s: hypotension), glucose (Cushing’s: hyperglycaemia); never stop steroids suddenly (adrenal crisis).

🔴 Hypoglycaemia treatment

Treat hypoglycaemia immediately with fast-acting sugar (glucose tablets, juice, sugar water) and recheck blood glucose in 15 minutes; repeat if still low.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Blood glucose monitoring — before meals and at bedtime; record and report abnormalities.
  • Insulin administration — check dose and type; rotate sites; check blood glucose before giving.
  • Hypoglycaemia — treat with fast-acting sugar; recheck in 15 minutes; educate patient/family.
  • Foot care — daily inspection, moisturise (not between toes), proper footwear, report cuts/infections.
  • Steroid therapy — never stop suddenly (adrenal crisis); monitor blood glucose, blood pressure, weight, mood.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Diabetes mellitus = high blood glucose (Type 1: no insulin; Type 2: insulin resistance).
  2. Classic symptoms: polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia (3Ps), weight loss, fatigue.
  3. Hypoglycaemia = low blood glucose; sweating, trembling, hunger, confusion, weakness — treat with fast-acting sugar.
  4. Hyperthyroidism = weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, fast pulse; hypothyroidism = weight gain, cold intolerance, fatigue.
  5. Cushing’s = excess cortisol (moon face, buffalo hump); Addison’s = cortisol deficiency (fatigue, weight loss, low BP).

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Insulin: rotate injection sites; check blood glucose before giving; do not mix unless compatible.
  2. Metformin: give with food; thyroxine: empty stomach in the morning.
  3. Steroids: never stop suddenly (adrenal crisis); monitor blood glucose, BP, weight.
  4. Diabetic foot care: daily inspection, moisturise, proper footwear, report cuts/infections.
  5. Thyroid storm = hyperthyroidism emergency (fever, tachycardia, agitation) — emergency.

📌 Memory trick

Diabetes classic symptoms: “3Ps” — Polyuria, Polydipsia, Polyphagia.

60-second revision

  • Endocrine disorders: diabetes, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, Cushing’s, Addison’s.
  • Diabetes: high blood glucose; 3Ps (polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia).
  • Hypoglycaemia = low blood glucose; treat with fast-acting sugar.
  • Thyroxine: empty stomach, morning; never stop steroids suddenly.
  • Diabetic foot care: daily inspection, moisturise, proper footwear.
  • Blood glucose monitoring before meals and at bedtime.

Test yourself

Type 1 diabetes is caused by:

Answer: B. Type 1 diabetes is autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells; little/no insulin produced.

Hypoglycaemia is treated with:

Answer: B. Hypoglycaemia (low blood glucose) is treated with fast-acting carbohydrates.

Thyroxine is taken:

Answer: B. Thyroxine is best absorbed on an empty stomach in the morning.

Cushing's syndrome features:

Answer: B. Cushing's syndrome (excess cortisol) causes moon face, buffalo hump, central obesity, thin skin, hypertension.

Addison's disease = adrenal insufficiency; danger is:

Answer: A. Addisonian crisis = life-threatening adrenal insufficiency with vomiting, dehydration, shock — emergency.
